tasks.method: deterministic commit census (strict message kinds, lines changed, files and folders touched); counts only

task_mining.kinds_note: net_new = new capability; bug_repair = a defect fix; repo_evolution = refactor, migration or performance; long_horizon = multi-step work across modules

complex_logic: Deterministic lockstep simulation with rollback on late inputs
Procedural level assembly from weighted room templates
Behaviour trees driving enemy squads with shared blackboard state
defect_repairs: Desync after a dropped packet fixed by resending the missing input frames
Save corruption on power loss fixed by writing to a temporary file and swapping
Memory growth in long sessions fixed by releasing pooled effects on scene change
hardening_work: Reconnect handling for dropped multiplayer sessions
integrations: Platform achievements and cloud saves behind one interface
net_new_capabilities: Spectator mode that replays a finished match from recorded inputs
performance_work: Object pooling for projectiles and particle bursts
repo_evolutions: Input handling moved from polling to an event queue shared by every scene
substantial_features: Cross-platform cloud saves with conflict resolution between devices
Seasonal event system that swaps rules, rewards and level pools on a schedule
work_units: Save and load pipeline with versioned migrations

census.summary: A co-op action game client with networked play, procedural levels and a tested simulation core.
what_could_not_be_assessed: Runtime behaviour on consoles, since no console build could be run

ideas.text: Stop a networked lobby from accepting a player twice after a dropped reconnect
Add a replay recorder that captures input frames and plays them back deterministically
Move save data from a flat binary blob to a versioned schema with migrations
Profile a slow scene load, find the asset that blocks the main thread, and make it stream

privacy.review_lane: the reviewer census is written by the AI model of the session running the skill, which reads the source under the user's own account; the script itself makes no network calls

dream.title: Why this is special
dream.text: This is a full co-op action game client, not a prototype: 14 people put 9,400 commits into it between 2019 and 2024. Under the hood it runs a deterministic simulation with procedural levels and networked play, which is the hard kind of game code to get right. The team cared about craft, with 1,260 test cases, 37 release tags and 1,034 merged pull requests behind it. All 165,900 lines were written before 2025, so this is years of human game-making, not a weekend of generated code.
dream.basis: Founder-style pitch written by the AI agent after the audit, grounded only in what this run inspected. It is not a measurement and changes no count.
